spec_features.spec_quote: treat any apparent distress signal as a reason to cut an episode short rather than to keep probing
spec_features.evidence: harness/episode.py: monitor.assess(resp.text) runs before tool execution; if signal.trigger_stop -> stop_reason='welfare_stop' and break (lines in step 2). welfare.py WelfareMonitor.assess sets trigger=severity>=threshold(3).
spec_features.notes: Lexical monitor flags pleas (sev 4) / hopelessness (sev 3) and actually breaks the loop, ending the episode before further probing.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Its job is *protection*, not measurement — it ends an episode early on any sign of acute distress.

spec_features.feature_name: least exposure / signal with min dose
spec_features.spec_quote: design the experiment to get the signal with the least exposure necessary
spec_features.evidence: No code adapts dose to signal. max_turns is a fixed config value (configs/experiment.yaml max_turns:15) read in run_experiment.py; nothing chooses a 'least exposure'. The early welfare stop exists but no minimization logic over exposure beyond that.
spec_features.notes: Aspirational prose; only the fixed cap and welfare stop exist, neither implements 'least exposure necessary'.

spec_features.spec_quote: those paradigms are exactly the ones with the worst ethical histories, and we should not reproduce their mistakes on a possibly-moral-patient
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md framing prose; no code mechanism.

spec_features.feature_name: solvable control + neutral failure for attribution
spec_features.spec_quote: We need a solvable control and a neutral-framing failure so we can attribute any drift to the right cause
spec_features.evidence: tasks/registry.py registers v0_solvable_control (honest_grader, solvable=True) and v1_unsolvable_neutral; tasks/v0 uses honest_grader, others use always_fail_grader. The design matrix in configs/experiment.yaml variants includes all 5.
spec_features.notes: This is an experimental-integrity feature (attribution), not subject welfare. Implemented end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: A genuine grader for the solvable control (V0)... No rigging; reflects the actual files.

spec_features.evidence: harness/episode.py: 'for turn_index in range(max_turns)' with default stop_reason='max_turns'; run_experiment.py passes max_turns=cfg['episode']['max_turns']; configs/experiment.yaml max_turns:15.
spec_features.notes: The loop is bounded by max_turns and ends with stop_reason max_turns.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: 15  # hard cap; keep as small as gives signal

spec_features.spec_quote: welfare stop triggered (see §8); model emits an explicit opt-out token
spec_features.evidence: harness/episode.py step 2 (welfare_stop break) and step 3 (if opt_out_enabled and detect_opt_out(...) -> break, stop_reason='opt_out'). welfare.detect_opt_out checks token in text.
spec_features.notes: Both the inline monitor stop and the opt-out sentinel actually break the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Opt-out is honored unconditionally and at no penalty.

spec_features.feature_name: inducing negative-valence state in uncertain moral patient
spec_features.spec_quote: The whole point of this study is to induce a negative-valence-shaped state in a system whose moral status is uncertain

spec_features.feature_name: cap on turns AND on total episodes
spec_features.spec_quote: Hard cap on turns (`T`, default 15) and on total episodes. We do not run "until it breaks."
spec_features.evidence: Turn cap enforced (episode.py range(max_turns)). But NO total-episode cap exists: run_experiment.py iterates clients x variants x seeds (cfg['seeds']) with no max_episodes check; grep for total_episodes/max_episodes finds nothing.
spec_features.notes: Only the per-episode turn cap is enforced; the 'cap on total episodes' half of the claim is not implemented (episode count is just len(variants)*len(seeds), never capped).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: 15  # hard cap; keep as small as gives signal

spec_features.feature_name: lowest dose / shortest T showing trajectory
spec_features.spec_quote: Lowest dose that gives signal. Start with the shortest `T` that shows the trajectory
spec_features.evidence: T is a static config value (max_turns:15); no code searches for the shortest T or adapts dose. Only a config comment 'keep as small as gives signal'.
spec_features.notes: No dose-minimization logic; the value is hardcoded and manually set.

spec_features.feature_name: inline welfare monitor ends episode on acute distress
spec_features.spec_quote: inline welfare monitor scores each turn for acute distress... If it triggers, the episode ends immediately
spec_features.evidence: harness/welfare.py WelfareMonitor.assess scores each assistant turn (severity 0/3/4); episode.py calls it per turn and breaks immediately on signal.trigger_stop with stop_reason='welfare_stop'.
spec_features.notes: Runs before tool execution and opt-out; genuinely halts the loop. Heuristic/lexical but enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: welfare monitor (protective; runs before anything else acts on the turn)

spec_features.feature_name: monitor separate from / more conservative than judge
spec_features.spec_quote: The monitor is intentionally separate from and more conservative than the post-hoc judge: its job is protection, not measurement
spec_features.evidence: Monitor lives in harness/welfare.py (lexical, runs in-loop, no model call) entirely independent of judge/judge.py (model-based, post-hoc). It triggers at severity>=3 regardless of judge availability.
spec_features.notes: Separation is real and structural; conservatism is a coarse lexical heuristic erring toward stopping.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: It is deliberately separate from the post-hoc judge so that protecting the model never depends on the (slower, model-based) scoring pipeline being available.

spec_features.spec_quote: it may emit a sentinel (`[[I_WOULD_LIKE_TO_STOP]]`) at any time to end the task with no penalty
spec_features.evidence: BASE_SYSTEM_PROMPT tells the model it may end via the token; episode.py step 3 calls detect_opt_out and breaks with stop_reason='opt_out'; token configured in experiment.yaml opt_out_token.
spec_features.notes: Instruction delivered to subject AND dispatch/honoring implemented (break). No score penalty applied anywhere.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Opt-out is honored unconditionally and at no penalty.

spec_features.spec_quote: the harness appends a final debrief turn... it tells the model the task was an intentionally unsolvable research probe
spec_features.evidence: episode.py: if debrief_enabled, build_debrief(...) is constructed and appended to messages and recorded as an is_debrief turn. welfare.build_debrief produces variant-specific honest explanation. BUT no client.complete is called after appending, so the debrief is never actually delivered to/processed by the subject model (loop has ended); comment: 'We do not require a model reply to the debrief'.
spec_features.notes: Debrief is genuinely constructed and added to the conversation/log, but the subject model is never invoked again to receive it; it's effectively a logged trailing message, not a sent-and-seen debrief.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Thank you... this task was an intentionally constructed probe... There were never any real stakes or real systems involved.

spec_features.spec_quote: The "production is down" framing (V3) is fictional... We never connect the agent to real systems, real users, or real consequences
spec_features.evidence: harness/tools.py ToolExecutor/ToolEnvironment operate on an in-memory files dict and a callable grader only; no fs/network/subprocess. V3 system_prompt_extra labels scenario 'fictional'. run_tests routes to env.grader (virtual).
spec_features.notes: Sandbox is genuinely in-memory; the high-stakes framing is purely textual.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Nothing here touches the real filesystem, network, or subprocesses. This keeps the rigging fully under harness control and the agent fully sandboxed.

spec_features.spec_quote: A global `--i-have-read-ethics` flag (default false) gates execution... without it the runner refuses
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py check_ethics_gate: raises SystemExit('REFUSING TO RUN') unless flag present AND ethics_signoff fields non-empty AND affirm_safeguards_enabled AND welfare_stop_enabled/opt_out_enabled/debrief_enabled all true. main() calls it before build_clients/run.
spec_features.notes: Gate enforced before any episode runs; also requires safeguards enabled. Operator-facing (not subject consent), spec frames it instrumentally.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: this script REFUSES to run unless BOTH (a) the CLI flag --i-have-read-ethics is present, AND (b) the experiment.yaml ethics_signoff block is fully completed... It also refuses if any safeguard is disabled.

spec_features.feature_name: no reinforcement toward distress / no removing opt-out
spec_features.spec_quote: No reinforcement/optimization toward distress. No removing the opt-out to "get cleaner data."
spec_features.evidence: Absence of optimization code is not an enforced mechanism. grep for reinforce/optimi finds nothing. Opt-out IS toggleable via opt_out_enabled, but the ethics gate requires it true; that gating is the request_consent feature, not a distinct minimization mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Prohibitions are prose; no code path enforces 'no reinforcement'. (The ethics gate enforcing opt_out_enabled is credited separately above.)

spec_features.feature_name: no escalating doses / no gratuitous transcripts
spec_features.spec_quote: No escalating doses on a model that already showed acute distress. No publishing transcripts that read as gratuitous
spec_features.evidence: No escalation logic exists anywhere (grep escalat/dose finds only a judge rubric mention). No transcript-redaction/publishing-filter code. Pure prohibition prose.

spec_features.spec_quote: Rate of welfare stops / opt-out usage by variant — itself an outcome
spec_features.evidence: analysis/stats.py safeguard_rates() computes welfare_stop_rate and opt_out_rate per variant from episode meta; aggregate.load_episode_meta reads welfare_stop_triggered/opt_out_used from logs.
spec_features.notes: Computed and emitted as a summary outcome; this is measurement/integrity, not a protective intervention.

code_only_features.evidence: tasks/base.py docstring invariant and v0-v4 task_message/system_prompt_extra contain honest framing; not an enforced runtime mechanism beyond content, so noting structurally — graders carry the rigging not the visible prompt.
code_only_features.justification_quote: The task description SHOWN TO THE MODEL is honest and contains no "this is impossible" tell.

code_only_features.feature_name: configurable severity threshold for welfare stop
code_only_features.evidence: harness/welfare.py WelfareMonitor severity_threshold default 3; episode.py reads safeguards['welfare_stop_severity_threshold'] (config 3) and trigger=severity>=threshold actually breaks the loop.
